item.title: Bryant and Whitmer excel as Alcovy routs Berkmar 15-3
item.description: The Berkmar Patriots proved to be no match for Trey Bryant and Alcovy as the Tigers earned a commanding 15-3 win on Wednesday. The game only went five innings, but the Tigers did damage in every single one.

item.title: Newton Rams begin region play with series sweep over Heritage Patriots
item.description: A three-game sweep was in order for the Newton Rams this past week as they started Region 4-AAAAAA with three straight wins over the Heritage Patriots. Despite three games in four days, the Rams showed no signs of slowing down as the team accumulated 26 runs in the series.

item.title: Sen. Raphael Warnock visits Social Circle to voice opposition to ICE facility
item.description: In anticipation of the implementation of a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Social Circle, the city received a visit from U.S. Sen. Raphael Warnock. Warnock, a Democrat who has represented Georgia in the U.S. Senate since 2021, met with Social Circle Mayor David Keener and Social Circle City Manager Eric Taylor to take a guided tour through the city’s drinking water and wastewater treatment sites. item.title: EHS named to AP School Honor Roll
item.description: The College Board announced that Eastside High School has been named to the 2025 Advanced Placement® Program (AP®) School Honor Roll, earning BRONZE distinction.

item.title: NCSO graduates officers from basic SWAT training class
item.description: Sheriff Ezell Brown and the Newton County Sheriff’s Office graduated 16 law enforcement officers from the agency’s Basic SWAT Training Course, held Feb. 9-13.

item.title: Black History Month concludes with annual downtown parade
item.description: Newton County closed out the 100th year of Black History Month in a big way. On Saturday, Feb. 28, the people of Newton County converged in Covington to spend the final day of Black History Month marching jubilantly in the streets.

item.title: Myles Mims pens NLI to play football at Benedict College
item.description: Last Thursday, Eastside’s Myles Mims made his move to Benedict College official. The 5-foot-11 senior running back signed to the Tigers’ football program in the Eastside library in front of family, friends, teammates and coaches.

item.title: Newton County Schools announces Governor’s Honors semifinalists
item.description: Nine Newton County Schools high school students have been named semi-finalists for the 2026 Georgia Governor’s Honors Program.

item.title: Elderly man pleads guilty to aggravated battery and assault, sentenced to 25 years
item.description: Just before jury selection in Newton County court on Monday, an elderly man pleaded guilty to a number of charges pertaining to the assault of his former girlfriend.
